newsitem.title: USA: J.C. Penney $2 bln debt said issue-bid.
newsitem.headline: J.C. Penney $2 bln debt said issue-bid.

text.p: All eyes are set on J.C. Penney Co Inc's $2.0 billion multi-tranche debt, which has already met with good demand and said to be issue-bid across the curve while in its pre-pricing stage, syndicate sources said on Tuesday.
"The deal is going very well...all tranches are issue-bid," said one high-grade syndicate source.
J.C. Penney's deal is expected to set the tone in the corporate bond primary market as players currently on the sidelines due to higher interest rates wait to see how the deal plays out.
"Right now its just wait-and-see...it's this 900 pound gorilla thats going to set the tone in the marketplace," another syndicate source said.
The deal consist of the following five tranches, syndicate sources said.
-$600 million in five-year debt with price talk seen between +45-50 basis points over U.S. Treasuries.
-$400 million in 10-year debt with price talk seen at +70 basis points over Treasuries.
-$300 million in 20-year bonds with price talk seen at +85 basis points.
-$350 million in 30-year debt, callable after 10 years, with price talk seen in the +120 basis points area.
-$350 million in 40-year bonds, putable in eight years, with price talk seen in the mid-40's.
Credit Suisse First Boston is expected to serve as lead underwriter for the offering.
Other players said the deal has room to grow as J.C. Penney currently has approximately $3.0 billion in debt on the shelf.
